This is a short tour: generate a study, look at its trial design, SDTM and ADaM, check it against
its targets, and write it out. The rest of the guide covers each step in depth.

## Generate a study

`tf.study()` takes an archetype (the study type), the number of subjects, a seed and the
archetype's controls. Here is a 12-week, placebo-controlled hypertension study with 300 subjects:

```{python}
import polars as pl
import trialforge as tf

trial = tf.study("parallel_continuous", n=300, seed=1, indication="hypertension", weeks=12)
trial
```

The result is a `Study`. Its summary gives the study identifier, the archetype, the seed and the
data cutoff (the date the study's data runs to), and lists every dataset: the trial design datasets
(TA, TE, TV, TI, TS), the SDTM domains, and the ADaM datasets derived from them. The study has
already passed trialforge's checks; a study that fails one is an error, never a result.

`n` is the number of randomized subjects. The seed makes the study reproducible: the same call
gives the same data every time, so the outputs on this page are what you will see too.

## The trial design

The trial design datasets describe the protocol rather than the subjects. TA (trial arms) lists
each arm's elements in order: screening, the arm's treatment, then follow-up:

```{python}
trial.sdtm["TA"].select("ARMCD", "ARM", "TAETORD", "ETCD", "ELEMENT", "EPOCH")
```

TV (trial visits) holds the planned visits, with the planned study day of each (`VISITDY`) and
its window. A subject who stops early has an `EARLY TERMINATION` visit, which has no planned day:

```{python}
trial.sdtm["TV"].filter(pl.col("ARMCD") == "PBO").select("VISITNUM", "VISIT", "VISITDY", "TVSTRL")
```

TS (trial summary) records the title, phase, indication, planned countries and the other facts a
registry would ask for, and TI the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

## Look at the SDTM

`trial.sdtm` maps domain names to DataFrames (Polars unless you pass `output="pandas"` or
`output="pyarrow"`). Demographics:

```{python}
trial.sdtm["DM"].select("USUBJID", "SUBJID", "SITEID", "AGE", "SEX", "RACE", "ARM", "RFSTDTC")
```

Each subject has a `SUBJID` made of the site number and the subject's order of enrollment at that
site (`201001` is the first subject at site 201), and a `USUBJID` that prefixes it with the study
identifier, so it is unique across studies. `RFSTDTC` is the date of first dose, which anchors the
study days (`--DY`) of every other domain: the day of first dose is day 1 and the day before it day
-1 (there is no day 0).

Adverse events are coded to MedDRA System Organ Class names and Preferred Terms:

```{python}
trial.sdtm["AE"].select("USUBJID", "AEDECOD", "AEBODSYS", "AESEV", "AESTDTC", "AEENDTC")
```

SDTM dates are ISO 8601 text, and a missing end date means the event was ongoing at the end of the
subject's participation (`AEENRTPT` says so).

## Look at the ADaM

`trial.adam` holds the analysis datasets, derived from the SDTM as admiral would derive them. One
subject's systolic blood pressure in ADVS, with its baseline and change from baseline:

```{python}
trial.adam["ADVS"].filter(
    pl.col("PARAMCD") == "SYSBP", pl.col("USUBJID") == "SIMPAR01-201001"
).select("TRTP", "AVISIT", "ADY", "AVAL", "BASE", "CHG", "ABLFL", "ANL01FL")
```

`ABLFL` marks the baseline record, the last value on or before the day of first dose, and `BASE`
carries it to every record; `CHG` is `AVAL - BASE` after baseline. `ANL01FL` marks the records an
analysis by visit should use: the baseline and, for each analysis visit, the one record closest to
the visit's planned day. Visits don't always happen on their planned day, so a subject can have two records in
the same analysis visit. This one stopped early, the day after their week 2 visit, and their
early termination measurements fall in the week 2 window too; the flag picks the one nearer day 15:

```{python}
trial.adam["ADVS"].filter(
    pl.col("PARAMCD") == "SYSBP", pl.col("USUBJID") == "SIMPAR01-218005"
).select("AVISIT", "ADY", "AVAL", "CHG", "ABLFL", "ANL01FL")
```

So filter on `ANL01FL == "Y"` to get one value per subject and visit. The mean change at week 12,
the end of treatment, by treatment:

```{python}
(
    trial.adam["ADVS"]
    .filter(pl.col("PARAMCD") == "SYSBP", pl.col("AVISIT") == "WEEK 12", pl.col("ANL01FL") == "Y")
    .group_by("TRTP", maintain_order=True)
    .agg(n=pl.len(), mean_chg=pl.col("CHG").mean().round(1))
)
```

Fewer than 150 subjects per arm have a week 12 value: the others discontinued before it.

## Compare targets with what was realized

The controls set the targets: the `hypertension` preset expects a mean change of -4 mmHg on placebo
and -12 mmHg on Drug A. The truth manifest reports those targets next to what this study's ADaM
shows:

```{python}
endpoint = trial.truth["endpoint"]
{k: endpoint[k] for k in ("target_difference", "realized_difference")}
```

With 300 subjects, the realized difference is close to the target but not equal to it, as in a real
study. The realized values are the means from the table above.

## Write it out

`write_submission()` writes a submission-style package: `sdtm/` and `adam/`, each with one XPT file
per dataset and a Define-XML 2.1 `define.xml`, plus `truth.json`:

```python
trial.write_submission("out/")
```

`write()` writes every dataset to one directory in any of the supported formats:

```{python}
tf.formats()
```
